title: Himalayan Cedar: Ancient Deodars You Can Visit
meta_description: Deodar means timber of the gods in the Himalaya. Padua's, planted in 1828, was the first deodar cultivated anywhere in Italy.
intro: Cedrus deodara comes from the western Himalaya, from Afghanistan through to Nepal, where deodar means timber of the gods and a tree can pass a thousand years. Every one here grows a very long way from those mountains. It reached Europe in 1822, and six years later Padua's Orto Botanico planted one that is still standing. The continent's park builders took to it at once: Florence's specimen was on the botanical garden's books by 1880, and Bergamo's stands alone in the middle of a lawn with its own lightning conductor, because it is the tallest thing for some distance. Austin's went in beside George Littlefield's house in 1893, and Tokyo's in Yanaka started as a pot plant at a bakery door around 1926. The drooping branch tips are the field mark that separates a deodar from the stiffer cedars of Lebanon and the Atlas.
